issues.where: shake, throughout the liquid, especially across the cottage, lower bowl and tree
issues.what: The candidate reads as a transparent cage of long straight hairlines with a few blurry blobs. The target is a bright, turbulent volume of short and long swishes, recognizable seed tufts, fine backlit haze and foreground streaks. The cottage, pond and ground stay too clearly outlined in the candidate.
issues.fix: Keep the settled crown and firefly color. Replace most of the continuous lines with shorter tapered streaks and filamented seeds at several focal depths, add luminous banks that sweep across the foreground and pool near the bottom, and increase occlusion between bursts of detail.

issues.where: both pairs, lower bowl and collar, crops 2 and 5
issues.what: The upper globe matches in diameter, but the candidate cuts its lower curve off higher. A broad chalky wedge above a dark gasket makes the landscape look like a flat insert sitting on top. In the target the lower glass rolls into a softly shaded rounded heel buried in the stone seat.
issues.fix: Let the bowl extend farther down, round and refract the terrain edge through the heel, and nest it into the stone with a narrow contact shadow instead of the exposed pale wedge and heavy black strip.

issues.where: both pairs, glass shoulders and side glare, crops 1 and 3
issues.what: The candidate glass reads as a smooth amber rim around a flat view. It loses the target's cool blue outer band and the separate sweeping reflections inside it. The lower-left glare becomes a flat white curtain instead of a compact, refracted flare.
issues.fix: Separate the cool outside reflection from the warm inner arcs, strengthen the curved distortion at the edges while keeping the center clearer, and localize the bright lower-left flare with a more gradual falloff.

issues.where: calm liquid above, beside and in front of the miniature
issues.what: Far more of the candidate is covered in tiny similarly focused dots, while the larger seeds are scarce and the space behind the miniature is comparatively dark and flat. The target has quieter pockets and a clearer near-to-far progression from soft beads and feathery forms to fine distant points.
issues.fix: Keep the settled yellow-green fireflies, seeds and gold motes, but thin the uniform dot layer, add a few larger readable seeds and soft close lights, and backlight the middle and lower depth with a warm volumetric veil.

issues.where: cottage roof, chimney and front, crop 2; also visible through the storm in B
issues.what: The candidate has a taller, darker brick chimney, a black roof with conspicuous orange stripes, and a bright angular plank door partly lost in vines. The target has a shorter gray stone chimney, a softly textured blue-black slate roof, an unmistakable rounded stone door arch and a visibly lit narrow window.
issues.fix: Bring the chimney and slate back to those proportions and colors, rebuild the weathered stone arch and warm window, and pull some of the foliage off the masonry so the architecture still reads.

issues.where: calm tree canopy, branches and trunk, crop 3
issues.what: The candidate canopy is flatter and more solid, with dark saturated stipple and angular branch junctions. The target has more distinct rounded tiers, airy gaps, warm edge light, and a broad curving trunk with visible grain.
issues.fix: Sculpt the intact canopy into more distinct rounded layers with small gaps, add warm raking light and softer foliage detail, and give the trunk and roots the target's taper, curvature and readable bark.

issues.where: paper lantern string and lamp post, crops 2 and 3
issues.what: The lanterns read as near-uniform orange globes with a flatter glow, and the post's pale square lamp lacks the target's warmer tapered silhouette. Their light does not tie the cottage and the tree together as strongly.
issues.fix: Bring back the variation in lantern size, paper ribs, warmer cores and darker caps, and give the post a tapered warm lantern with localized spill onto the grass and water.

issues.where: fence, grass and planted edges on both sides of the pond, crops 2 and 5
issues.what: The left fence is a nearly black, dense barrier and the banks look like even bristles with separately placed sunflowers. The target has an open, warm rail fence, irregular low moss and pale tufted cover catching the backlight, and more naturally grouped flowers.
issues.fix: Open and warm the fence rails, break up the grass edge with mounded moss and fine lit tufts, and vary flower heights, tilts and spacing.

issues.where: pond, path and shore, crops 2 and 5
issues.what: The pond is still recognizable, but it has harsh upright white reflection bars and a very regular pebble border. The target has a lower, softer warm mirror with legible lamp and trunk silhouettes, and a less repetitive stone approach blending into the bank.
issues.fix: Reorient and soften the warm reflections around the actual lamp and trunk silhouettes, and replace the uniform trim with a few more varied stones embedded in the grass and path.

issues.where: both pairs, pedestal body and foot, crops 4 and 6
issues.what: The base is taller and more regular, with a rolled foot and broadly uniform sandy cement color. The target is a lower, more irregular stone pedestal with weathered layers, cool blue-gray shadows and sharply raked warm ridges.
issues.fix: Keep the deeper carving, but lower the profile and break up the foot, add directional layered stone texture, and restore the split between cool shadow and localized amber highlights.

issues.where: both pairs, shell and glass details on the pedestal, crops 4 to 6
issues.what: The added pieces are not the issue. Many are flat opaque colored inserts or soft molded reliefs, rather than raised shells and rounded translucent sea glass with substantial contact shadows and glints.
issues.fix: Keep the extra pieces and vary their relief, rib detail, contact shadows and the translucency and edge lighting of the glass.

issues.where: both pairs, external sand and tabletop reflection, crops 5 and 6
issues.what: Beyond the approved soft light pool, the surface is broadly tan and the base reflection is a smeary warm stripe instead of a dark, tighter wet sheen under the foot. The right-side sand reads as detached spray and evenly scattered bright grains beside a smooth dune rather than as a small spill down into an irregular grounded pile.
issues.fix: Keep the approved pool and bands, restore the darker reflective tabletop and tight foot contact, and give the sand a finer continuous fall with a more broken mound and believable contact shadows.

issues.where: both pairs, background bokeh and color contrast around the globe
issues.what: The background compresses into a flat navy field with a broad brown blob well inside the left and a couple of isolated round lights at upper right. The target has brighter edge-hugging warm bokeh clustered at the right and a cooler teal-black backdrop, reinforcing the warm backlight and cool shadows on the globe and stone.
issues.fix: Keep the smooth background, but move the brightest warm bokeh toward the edges, restore the clustered falloff at upper right and along the reflective right side, and bring back the cooler ambient fill.
